meta.disclaimer: Not legal advice. These are counts of veterans already receiving VA disability compensation, not claims, appeals or unmet need: a rating says how VA scored a service-connected condition, not whether a veteran needs a lawyer or could get a higher rating. Questions about a claim are for an accredited attorney, agent or veterans service officer.
meta.notice: Probative is a marketing firm, not a law firm; not legal advice.

records.note: Every row of VA's file: the counties, Puerto Rico, the other territories, veterans abroad and unknown addresses. VA's Annual Benefits Report counts 6,338,253 compensation recipients at the end of FY 2025; the county file leaves out the few veterans in suppressed county totals and is built from a different address source.
records.text: United States: 6,331,627 veterans received VA disability compensation on September 30, 2025 (FY 2025) (at least; some county counts are suppressed). By combined rating: 1,845,855 rated 100%, 1,868,474 rated 70% to 90%, 728,907 at 50% to 60%, 663,882 at 30% to 40% and 1,218,210 at 0% to 20%. 6,299 recipients sit in rating cells VA suppressed to protect privacy. A year earlier (FY 2024): 5,985,189 (+346,438).
